messages:
maria: Quick results from today's quant bake — AWQ INT8 vs FP8 on rwd-7b-chat with prefix cache + continuous-batcher. Short summary: AWQ INT8 ~3% eval delta on LLM-eval-set but we see a 12-18% effective latency regression in production when prefix cache is enabled. Details below. :thinking_face:

maria: Key observations:
- p50 increased ~15ms, p95/p99 jumped more (see perf-bot snapshot).
- KV cache hit-rate drops from ~86% -> ~62% for long-prefixed chats when we include quant_tag in the cache key.
- Continuous batcher sees more small batches (pack failures) because cached prefix lengths become fragmented across quant variants.

maria: Minimal repro logs:
```
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 model=rwd-7b-chat quant=awq-int8 prefix_hash=0x7af len_pref=512 cache_hit=false pack_attempt=1 batch_size=1
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] req_id=abc124 model=rwd-7b-chat quant=fp8 prefix_hash=0x7af len_pref=512 cache_hit=true pack_attempt=2 batch_size=8
```
(we saw same prefix_hash but different quant tags -> separate cache entries)

devin: This is expected if cache_key includes quant_tag. Current key: `cache_key = f"{model}:{quant}:{prefix_hash}:{client_id}"`.
Proposal: normalize quant tag for cache key (map all compatible quant variants to a shared tag) OR add a compatibility-mapping layer so different quant variants read the same KV if binary-compatible.

devin: Example patch idea:
```
# normalize quant profile for cache key
quant_group = quant.normalize_group()  # awq-int8|gptq-int8 -> int8-shared
cache_key = f"{model}:{quant_group}:{prefix_hash}:{client_id}"
```
Would need to prove bit-compatibility and ensure fallback if mismatch.

jin: Heads-up: we saw small but consistent accuracy regressions on AWQ INT8 for long-history prompts even when logits are similar. If we reuse FP8 cache for AWQ outputs you may hide subtle numeric drift. Need targeted evals on prompt-length buckets (0-128, 128-512, 512-2048).

jin: Suggest running a 48h A/B with two policies:
- shared-prefetch (share cache across quant variants, but tag entries with provenance and do checksum on KV shape)
- isolated-prefetch (current behavior)
Measure: cache-hit-rate by prefix-length, p50/p95, and task-level accuracy on our promptset.

sam: Also looks like continuous-batcher thresholds amplify the issue. When cache hit fails, requests become small and don't wait to aggregate -> more overhead. Two quick knobs to try: raise `max_batch_delay_ms` from 8->12 for chat bursts, and increase `min_batch_tokens` so we don't send tiny batches. Will try canary.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (canary window 10:00-11:00):
- baseline (fp8, shared cache): p50=95ms p95=340ms p99=520ms cache_hit=86%
- awq-int8 (isolated cache): p50=110ms p95=450ms p99=660ms cache_hit=62%
- small-batch-rate +23% (pack failures), qps -3%

maria: Good. Also found a small bug: our prefix cache key uses `len_pref` in bytes for quantized models instead of token count, causing mis-grouping when the quantized weight representation differs. That explains some fragmentation. Fix: compute key with `prefix_token_count` only.

devin: +1 to token-count normalization. For mapping quant groups we need a safety net: checksum KV on read and fallback to recompute KV if mismatch. That keeps correctness though increases first-request cost.

jin: For evals — add a hallucination metric focusing on LLM-eval-set subsets with long context and supervised QA. I volunteer to run the 48h A/B and push results to the deck.

sam: I'll spin a canary with:
- normalize token-based cache key
- quant_group mapping for AWQ/GPTQ -> int8-shared (opt-in)
- bump continuous-batcher `max_batch_delay_ms` to 12ms
Target rollout: canary to 5% traffic in eng/staging by EOD.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed: branch=batcher-prefetch-stability -> 5% (eng/staging). CI: green.

maria: Action items:
- devin: implement quant_group mapping + checksum fallback (PR)
- jin: run 48h A/B evals and report accuracy/hallucination by prefix-length buckets
- sam: monitor pack-failure rate and latency during canary, revert threshold if p95 regresses >10%

maria: FYI, if shared-cache approach proves safe we can save ~12-18% effective latency in mixed-quant fleets, so worth the extra eval rigor. :eyes:
